subject: The biggest mistake punters make at Cheltenham
preview_text: Everyone believes this handicapping rule is gospel. Our AI just proved it's costing you money. The truth inside.
body_paragraphs: Let's talk about Cheltenham. Or any major festival. There's one piece of advice shouted from every rooftop, repeated in every pub, and scribbled on every napkin: 'Always back the horse that won last time out.' It feels solid. It feels safe. It's also completely, provably wrong for the big races.

We ran the data. Across the last five years of major UK & Irish festivals, horses coming off a win actually underperform their predicted odds by nearly 18% in championship-level races. The pressure, the step up in class, the different track configuration—it crushes them. Everyone's chasing last week's form, blind to the real contender quietly building in the background. Your gut, the tipsters, the crowd... they're all stuck in the same loop.

This is where Predictify stops the guesswork. Our AI doesn't get sentimental about a recent win. It weighs the jockey's festival experience, the trainer's performance under pressure, and how the horse's speed ratings hold up against stiffer competition. It finds the horse that's peaking NOW, not the one that already peaked. That's the edge in your pocket.

Open the app. Go to the Cheltenham racecard. Look for the horse with the high confidence score that *didn't* win its last outing. See the variables our AI prioritized. That's your proof. Try it with Premium for 3 days—see every data point behind the pick. P.S. The favourite for the Champion Hurdle? It lost its last prep race. Our model still has it top three. That's the kind of contrarian insight that wins.
